actions.added_meaning: Selected exact House tips and overtime deduction/identification clauses follow. House 110101 deduction and reporting gate: There shall be allowed as a deduction an amount equal to the qualified tips received during the taxable year that are included on statements furnished to the individual pursuant to section 6041(d)(3), 6041A(e)(3), 6050W(f)(2), 6051(a)(18), or reported by the taxpayer on Form 4137 (or successor). House 110101 business receipt/expense limit: In the case of qualified tips received by an individual during any taxable year in the course of any trade or business of such individual, such qualified tips shall be taken into account under subsection (a) only to the extent that the gross receipts of the taxpayer from such trade or business for such taxable year (including such qualified tips) exceeds the sum of-- (1) cost of goods sold that are allocable to such receipts, plus (2) other expenses, losses, or deductions (other than the deduction allowed under this section), which are properly allocable to such receipts. House 110101 qualified-tip conditions: For purposes of this section-- (1) In general.--The term `qualified tip' means any cash tip received by an individual in an occupation which traditionally and customarily received tips on or before December 31, 2024, as provided by the Secretary. (2) Exclusions.--Such term shall not include any amount received by an individual unless-- (A) such amount is paid voluntarily without any consequence in the event of nonpayment, is not the subject of negotiation, and is determined by the payor, (B) the trade or business in the course of which the individual receives such amount is not a specified service trade or business (as defined in section 199A(d)(2)), (C) such individual does not receive earned income (within the meaning of section 32) in excess of the dollar amount in effect under section 414(q)(1)(B)(i) for the calendar year in which the taxable year begins, and (D) such other requirements as may be established by the Secretary in regulations or other guidance are satisfied. House 110101 identification and own marital rules: (1) In general.--No deduction shall be allowed under this section unless the taxpayer includes on the return of tax for the taxable year-- (A) such individual's social security number, and (B) if the individual is married, the social security number of such individual's spouse. (2) Married individuals.--Rules similar to the rules of section 32(d) shall apply to this section. (3) Social security number defined.--For purposes of paragraph (1), the term `social security number' shall have the meaning given such term in section 24(h)(7).. House 110101 anti-reclassification regulations: The Secretary shall prescribe such regulations or other guidance as may be necessary to prevent reclassification of income as qualified tips, including regulations or other guidance to prevent abuse of the deduction allowed by this section. House 110101 deduction termination: No deduction shall be allowed under this section for any taxable year beginning after December 31, 2028.. [[Page H2301]] House 110101 non-itemizer deduction: Section 63(b) is amended by striking and at the end of paragraph (3), by striking the period at the end of paragraph (4) and inserting and, and by adding at the end the following new paragraph: (5) the deduction provided in section 224.. House 110101 math-error amendment: Section 6213(g)(2), as amended by the preceding provisions of this Act, is amended by striking and at the end of subparagraph (V), by striking the period at the end of subparagraph (W) and inserting , and, and by inserting after subparagraph (W) the following new subparagraph: (X) an omission of a correct social security number required under section 224(d) (relating to deduction for qualified tips).. House 110101 tax-year applicability: The amendments made by this section shall apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024. House 110102 deduction: There shall be allowed as a deduction an amount equal to the qualified overtime compensation received during the taxable year. House 110102 qualified-overtime conditions: (1) In general.--For purposes of this section, the term `qualified overtime compensation' means overtime compensation paid to an individual required under section 7 of the Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938 that is in excess of the regular rate (as used in such section) at which such individual is employed. (2) Exclusions.--Such term shall not include-- (A) any qualified tip (as defined in section 224(c)), or (B) any amount received by an individual during a taxable year if such individual is a highly compensated employee (as defined in section 414(q)(1)) of any employer for the calendar year in which the taxable year begins, or receives earned income in excess of the dollar amount in effect under section 414(q)(1)(B)(i) for such calendar year. House 110102 identification and own marital rules: (1) In general.--No deduction shall be allowed under this section unless the taxpayer includes on the return of tax for the taxable year-- (A) such individual's social security number, and (B) if the individual is married, the social security number of such individual's spouse. (2) Married individuals.--Rules similar to the rules of section 32(d) shall apply to this section. (3) Social security number defined.--For purposes of paragraph (1), the term `social security number' shall have the meaning given such term in section 24(h)(7).. House 110102 regulations: The Secretary shall issue such regulations or other guidance as may be necessary or appropriate to carry out the purposes of this section. House 110102 deduction termination: No deduction shall be allowed under this section for any taxable year beginning after December 31, 2028.. House 110102 non-itemizer deduction: Section 63(b), as amended by the preceding provisions of this Act, is amended by striking and at the end of paragraph (4), by striking the period at the end of paragraph (5) and inserting and, and by adding at the end the following new paragraph: (6) the deduction provided in section 225.. House 110102 math-error amendment: Section 6213(g)(2), as amended by the preceding provisions of this Act, is amended by striking and at the end of subparagraph (W), by striking the period at the end of subparagraph (X) and inserting , and, and by inserting after subparagraph (X) the following new subparagraph: (Y) an omission of a correct social security number required under section 225(c) (relating to deduction for qualified overtime).. House 110102 tax-year applicability: The amendments made by this section shall apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024. These provisions allow deductions for their own qualified income, not exemption of every dollar described colloquially as tips or overtime and not a guarantee of zero tax. Each retains the complete printed qualified-income gates and its own new statutory subsection references; statements/Form 4137 references, business net-income limits, exceptions and regulatory instructions are not omitted. The original 199A(d)(2) service-business definition is bound with its own 1202/475 references, without importing the separate 199A(d)(3) qualified-business-income phase-in as an automatic tips exception or classifying an actual profession. Overtime means compensation required under FLSA section 7 in excess of the regular rate, not all compensation for hours described as overtime or a taxpayer employment determination. Complete original section 7 with common applicability, regular-rate inclusions/exclusions, alternative arrangements, compensatory-time and other own limitations is bound; no universal 40-hour or all-worker eligibility claim is inferred. All four SSN definitions use their own same-bill 24(h)(7) and full SSA issuance route: citizen or specified authorization, issued before the return due date, not every SSN or a citizen-only rule. Neither a valid number nor filing alone establishes the deduction. Own non-itemizer allowance and math-error amendment remain distinct from existing notice, conditional 60-day abatement-request and deficiency procedure; no actual assessment/fraud determination. All four deduction sections apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024, and deny deductions for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2028; tax-year language is not a discharge/event deadline or repeal of all related reporting/business-credit rules. Other financial/reporting context remains in complete source bindings without an actual implementation conclusion. Other H.R.1 components and separately reserved questions remain unfinished. House tips and overtime require taxpayer SSN and a spouse SSN if married, plus rules similar to 32(d). Full joint-return default and separated-spouse exception retain qualifying-child residence and alternative abode/decree/household conjunctions; actual adaptation to these deductions is reserved as question 58, not a universal child/joint-return requirement. House tips retains its earned-income-above-414(q)(1)(B)(i) exclusion, while overtime separately excludes qualified tips and highly compensated employees or above-threshold earned income. Full original 414(q) definition, its preceding-year/employer-election/ownership/adjustment/coordination and nonresident-alien context, plus 32(c)(2) earned-income definition and exclusions are bound. No fixed unadjusted $80,000 threshold or actual employee/income classification is inferred. House does not print the Senate $25,000 tips or $12,500/$25,000 overtime deduction caps/MAGI phaseout, and those are not imported. House inserts math-error (X) for tips and (Y) for overtime. The floor prints an extra closing quote/period immediately after each SSN-definition clause; served EH omits those delimiters while remaining operative words match after separately declared display normalization. Governing floor bytes remain unchanged; effect of those boundaries and reliable rendering/application is question 59, without retroactively replacing the vote-time text.

actions.added_meaning: Selected exact Senate tips and overtime deduction/identification clauses follow. Senate 70201 deduction and reporting gate: There shall be allowed as a deduction an amount equal to the qualified tips received during the taxable year that are included on statements furnished to the individual pursuant to section 6041(d)(3), 6041A(e)(3), 6050W(f)(2), or 6051(a)(18), or reported by the taxpayer on Form 4137 (or successor). Senate 70201 amount and income limits: (1) In general.--The amount allowed as a deduction under this section for any taxable year shall not exceed $25,000. (2) Limitation based on adjusted gross income.-- (A) In general.--The amount allowable as a deduction under subsection (a) (after application of paragraph (1)) shall be reduced (but not below zero) by $100 for each $1,000 by which the taxpayer's modified adjusted gross income exceeds $150,000 ($300,000 in the case of a joint return). (B) Modified adjusted gross income.--For purposes of this paragraph, the term `modified adjusted gross income' means the adjusted gross income of the taxpayer for the taxable year increased by any amount excluded from gross income under section 911, 931, or 933. Senate 70201 non-employee business-income limit: In the case of qualified tips received by an individual during any taxable year in the course of a trade or business (other than the trade or business of performing services as an employee) of such individual, such qualified tips shall be taken into account under subsection (a) only to the extent that the gross income for the taxpayer from such trade or business for such taxable year (including such qualified tips) exceeds the sum of the deductions (other than the deduction allowed under this section) allocable to the trade or business in which such qualified tips are received by the individual for such taxable year. Senate 70201 qualified-tip conditions: For purposes of this section-- (1) In general.--The term `qualified tips' means cash tips received by an individual in an occupation which customarily and regularly received tips on or before December 31, 2024, as provided by the Secretary. (2) Exclusions.--Such term shall not include any amount received by an individual unless-- (A) such amount is paid voluntarily without any consequence in the event of nonpayment, is not the subject of negotiation, and is determined by the payor, (B) the trade or business in the course of which the individual receives such amount is not a specified service trade or business (as defined in section 199A(d)(2)), and (C) such other requirements as may be established by the Secretary in regulations or other guidance are satisfied. For purposes of subparagraph (B), in the case of an individual receiving tips in the trade or business of performing services as an employee, such individual shall be treated as receiving tips in the course of a trade or business which is a specified service trade or business if the trade or business of the employer is a specified service trade or business. (3) Cash tips.--For purposes of paragraph (1), the term `cash tips' includes tips received from customers that are paid in cash or charged and, in the case of an employee, tips received under any tip-sharing arrangement. Senate 70201 identification: (1) In general.--No deduction shall be allowed under this section unless the taxpayer includes on the return of tax for the taxable year such individual's social security number. (2) Social security number defined.--For purposes of paragraph (1), the term `social security number' shall have the meaning given such term in section 24(h)(7). Senate 70201 own married-individual joint-return rule: If the taxpayer is a married individual (within the meaning of section 7703), this section shall apply only if the taxpayer and the taxpayer's spouse file a joint return for the taxable year. Senate 70201 anti-reclassification regulations: The Secretary shall prescribe such regulations or other guidance as may be necessary to prevent reclassification of income as qualified tips, including regulations or other guidance to prevent abuse of the deduction allowed by this section. Senate 70201 deduction termination: No deduction shall be allowed under this section for any taxable year beginning after December 31, 2028.. Senate 70201 non-itemizer deduction: Section 63(b) is amended by striking and at the end of paragraph (3), by striking the period at the end of paragraph (4) and inserting , and, and by adding at the end the following new paragraph: (5) the deduction provided in section 224.. Senate 70201 math-error amendment: Section 6213(g)(2), as amended by the preceding provisions of this Act, is amended by striking and at the end of subparagraph (W), by striking the period at the end of subparagraph (X) and inserting , and, and by inserting after subparagraph (X) the following new subparagraph: (Y) an omission of a correct social security number required under section 224(e) (relating to deduction for qualified tips).. Senate 70201 tax-year applicability: The amendments made by this section shall apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024. Senate 70202 deduction and reporting gate: There shall be allowed as a deduction an amount equal to the qualified overtime compensation received during the taxable year and included on statements furnished to the individual pursuant to section 6041(d)(4) or 6051(a)(19). Senate 70202 amount and income limits: (1) In general.--The amount allowed as a deduction under this section for any taxable year shall not exceed $12,500 ($25,000 in the case of a joint return). (2) Limitation based on adjusted gross income.-- (A) In general.--The amount allowable as a deduction under subsection (a) (after application of paragraph (1)) shall be reduced (but not below zero) by $100 for each $1,000 by which the taxpayer's modified adjusted gross income exceeds $150,000 ($300,000 in the case of a joint return). (B) Modified adjusted gross income.--For purposes of this paragraph, the term `modified adjusted gross income' means the adjusted gross income of the taxpayer for the taxable year increased by any amount excluded from gross income under section 911, 931, or 933. Senate 70202 qualified-overtime conditions: (1) In general.--For purposes of this section, the term `qualified overtime compensation' means overtime compensation paid to an individual required under section 7 of the Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938 that is in excess of the regular rate (as used in such section) at which such individual is employed. (2) Exclusions.--Such term shall not include any qualified tip (as defined in section 224(d)). Senate 70202 identification: (1) In general.--No deduction shall be allowed under this section unless the taxpayer includes on the return of tax for the taxable year such individual's social security number. (2) Social security number defined.--For purposes of paragraph (1), the term `social security number' shall have the meaning given such term in section 24(h)(7). Senate 70202 own married-individual joint-return rule: If the taxpayer is a married individual (within the meaning of section 7703), this section shall apply only if the taxpayer and the taxpayer's spouse file a joint return for the taxable year. Senate 70202 regulations: The Secretary shall issue such regulations or other guidance as may be necessary or appropriate to carry out the purposes of this section, including regulations or other guidance to prevent abuse of the deduction allowed by this section. Senate 70202 deduction termination: No deduction shall be allowed under this section for any taxable year beginning after December 31, 2028.. Senate 70202 non-itemizer deduction: Section 63(b), as amended by the preceding provisions of this Act, is amended by striking and at the end of paragraph (4), by striking the period at the end of paragraph (5) and inserting , and, and by adding at the end the following new paragraph: (6) the deduction provided in section 225.. Senate 70202 math-error amendment: Section 6213(g)(2), as amended by the preceding provisions of this Act, is amended by striking and at the end of subparagraph (X), by striking the period at the end of subparagraph (Y) and inserting , and, and by inserting after subparagraph (Y) the following new subparagraph: (Z) an omission of a correct social security number required under section 225(d) (relating to deduction for qualified overtime).. Senate 70202 tax-year applicability: The amendments made by this section shall apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024. These provisions allow deductions for their own qualified income, not exemption of every dollar described colloquially as tips or overtime and not a guarantee of zero tax. Each retains the complete printed qualified-income gates and its own new statutory subsection references; statements/Form 4137 references, business net-income limits, exceptions and regulatory instructions are not omitted. The original 199A(d)(2) service-business definition is bound with its own 1202/475 references, without importing the separate 199A(d)(3) qualified-business-income phase-in as an automatic tips exception or classifying an actual profession. Overtime means compensation required under FLSA section 7 in excess of the regular rate, not all compensation for hours described as overtime or a taxpayer employment determination. Complete original section 7 with common applicability, regular-rate inclusions/exclusions, alternative arrangements, compensatory-time and other own limitations is bound; no universal 40-hour or all-worker eligibility claim is inferred. All four SSN definitions use their own same-bill 24(h)(7) and full SSA issuance route: citizen or specified authorization, issued before the return due date, not every SSN or a citizen-only rule. Neither a valid number nor filing alone establishes the deduction. Own non-itemizer allowance and math-error amendment remain distinct from existing notice, conditional 60-day abatement-request and deficiency procedure; no actual assessment/fraud determination. All four deduction sections apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024, and deny deductions for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2028; tax-year language is not a discharge/event deadline or repeal of all related reporting/business-credit rules. Other financial/reporting context remains in complete source bindings without an actual implementation conclusion. Other H.R.1 components and separately reserved questions remain unfinished. Senate tips and overtime require taxpayer SSN, without a separately printed House spouse-SSN condition or similar-32(d) addition. Each independently requires a joint return if the taxpayer is married within 7703. Complete original 7703 retains end-of-year or death timing, legal-separation rule and its living-apart alternative requiring a separate return, own household/child/dependency conditions, over-half household costs and no spouse membership during the final six months. No blanket joint filing for every person colloquially described as married. Senate tips caps deduction at $25,000; overtime at $12,500 or $25,000 for a joint return, each with $100 per $1,000 over $150,000/$300,000 MAGI phaseout and own 911/931/933 additions. Senate tips uses own cash/charged/tip-sharing and employee/employer service-business clauses; overtime excludes qualified tips, without importing House highly-compensated/earned-income exclusions. Senate inserts math-error (Y) for tips and (Z) for overtime. No House spouse, similar-marital, compensation-threshold, extra-quote or distinct qualified-tip subsection rule is borrowed.
